questions.text: How is your target market defined and sized?

A.text: No specific target segment defined; no sizing method used

B.text: Target segment loosely defined; sizing is a single estimate with no stated method

C.text: Segment clearly and specifically defined; one sizing method used (bottom-up or top-down) with assumptions stated

D.text: Clearly defined segment; sizing uses credible external sources with assumptions documented

E.text: Clearly defined segment; sizing triangulates independent methods that corroborate each other, assumptions documented and sourced, revisited periodically

questions.text: What is your strongest evidence that customers will choose and pay for your specific solution?

A.text: No direct contact with potential customers; belief rests on assumption

B.text: Informal conversations show interest, but the cost or urgency of the problem is unconfirmed

C.text: Documented conversations with customers representative of the target segment confirm the problem is real and worth solving; willingness to pay untested

D.text: Representative customers have expressed specific purchase intent (letter of intent, pilot agreement, deposit) but no revenue collected

E.text: Representative customers have actually paid, across more than one independent relationship

questions.text: What makes customers choose this business over alternatives, and how hard would that be for a competitor to copy?

A.text: No articulated reason for a customer to choose this business over alternatives, including doing nothing

B.text: A reason exists but is weak or easily matched, not supported by research or customer input

C.text: A meaningful difference exists — supported by customer/problem research or direct customer confirmation — but is realistically copyable

D.text: A meaningful difference is backed by a structural defensibility factor: switching cost, proprietary process or data, exclusive access, brand trust, network effect, or cost advantage

E.text: Multiple differentiators clearly articulated and supported by customer/problem research, protected through more than one structural mechanism

questions.text: How well does the business understand its market conditions and respond to them?

A.text: No awareness of market conditions and no deliberate response — purely reactive

B.text: A general impression exists, but no deliberate response is in motion

C.text: Conditions understood with some rigor (sourced, not impression); a response plan exists but is not fully executed

D.text: Conditions understood with rigor, and a deliberate strategy suited to them is actively being executed

E.text: As D, with evidence the strategy is working (a trending measure moving as intended), or — pre-revenue — the strategy is visibly reflected in core product and positioning decisions made because of this market read

questions.text: Do you have an identified, repeatable way of reaching new customers?

A.text: No identifiable method — customers arrive coincidentally or not at all

B.text: A method has been tried or planned but has not shown it can reliably reach the target segment

C.text: A specific channel reliably reaches and engages the target segment, even before converting to paying customers

D.text: A specific channel repeatedly converts reached prospects into active users or pilot participants, and the business can explain why it works

E.text: More than one channel has repeatedly demonstrated strong engagement from the target segment, reducing dependence on a single route

questions.text: What evidence do you have that customers stay engaged, return, or advocate for your business over time?

REVENUE_GENERATING.text: What evidence do you have that customers stay engaged, return, or advocate for your business over time?

A.text: No evidence of continued relationship or advocacy

B.text: Isolated positive signals but no pattern across customers

C.text: A pattern of continued relationship exists across multiple customers — repeat purchase, renewal, extension, follow-on work, or unprompted positive feedback, whichever is natural to the business — but is not tracked

D.text: That pattern is consistently tracked across the customers relevant to the business's natural engagement cycle

E.text: The tracked pattern includes active advocacy — referrals, testimonials, references — that measurably contributes to new business

PRE_REVENUE.text: What evidence do you have that people who have engaged with your concept remain engaged, or would vouch for it?

A.text: No one has stayed engaged or been willing to vouch beyond an initial conversation

B.text: A few isolated people remain informally engaged; nothing sustained

C.text: A defined group — design partners, waitlist, pilot testers — has stayed engaged across multiple touchpoints

D.text: That group has proactively re-engaged: extended a pilot, referred someone, agreed to a reference call

E.text: Independent people or organisations have proactively advocated without being asked
